text:
Lina: @channel PRD intake — minimal shipping spec for deterministic tenant fallback when primary model variant is degraded/unavailable.

Problem: customers see 5xx/timeout errors or large latency spikes when the preferred model is rate-limited or OOMs. We need a well-scoped fallback contract so apps can stay online without manual intervention.

High-level goals:
- Define exact routing policy (priority list + eligibility checks) for per-request fallbacks.
- Acceptance criteria and automated checks (quality, latency, safety).
- Rollout plan: canary + per-tenant opt-in and metrics to detect regressions.

Non-goals:
- Reworking global rate limiter or billing model.
- Full multi-tenant QoS surface (we'll use simple tenant-level flags for now).

Success metrics (initial):
- Reduce user-facing 5xx/timeouts from fallback-eligible requests by >= 60%.
- Median latency change for successful fallbacks <= +30ms; p95 <= +100ms.
- Quality regression on core eval set < 3% (per-intent accuracy / BLEU-like metric).

Acceptance criteria (dev ready):
- Routing logic implemented behind a feature flag.
- Tracing tags emitted: `fallback.used`, `fallback.variant`, `fallback.reason`.
- Metrics: `fallback.count`, `fallback.quality.delta`, `fallback.error_rate` in Console.
- Eval harness runbook: scriptable test that runs 10k prompts and returns quality delta + CI gate.

Edge cases to call out:
- Streaming responses: if primary fails mid-stream, how do we stitch fallback output without protocol break? (risk: duplicate tokens / continuity).
- KV cache / cache keys: fallback variant may have different tokenization/kv layout -> risk of incoherent completions.
- Per-tenant opt-out/opt-in and persistence of preference.

Timeline ask: 2 working days to finalize acceptance criteria + owners, then 2 weeks spec -> 4 week dev sprint estimated.

Owners requested: runtime + platform + product review. Please call out missing items or blockers.

Ravi: Quick Q — quality regression target: when you say <3% is that relative to rank-1 quality on our core eval set or absolute threshold? Also want to confirm whether we allow semantic fallback (i.e., switch to reranker-only flow) or only lower-capacity variants.

Marta: I think call it relative to each intent's baseline; absolute thresholds will vary too much. Also we need a simple per-tenant flag stored in tenant config (boolean + preferred fallback order). Not a full UI yet.

Sam: Agree on metrics. Suggest adding `fallback.latency.delta` (histogram) and a per-tenant daily regression alert if `fallback.quality.delta` > 3% for 24h. Also will add Console dashboard template.

Ian: Heads-up on streaming + KV cache — if we attempt mid-stream fallback we should prefer terminating and returning a clear error to client or require client to support resume. Stitching is risky. Also: ensure KV cache invalidation path documented; otherwise we can leak state across variants.

Marta: +1 on not stitching mid-stream for initial launch. Simpler route: fail-fast and return structured error suggesting retry with fallback.

Lina: Good callouts. Updated items: make mid-stream fallback a hard non-goal for launch (we'll add RFC for streaming stitching later). Keep per-tenant fallback order as config.

OpsBot: Created doc: https://rwd.internal/doc/PRD-1729987654 (draft). Linked PR: https://git.internal/redwood/inference/pulls/1234. Template reminder: use "fallbacks-spec-v1" checklist.

Ravi: I'll draft the eval harness artifacts (prompt sets + scoring) by EOD tomorrow.

Sam: I'll own metrics + dashboard (ETA 3d).

Marta: I'll own tenant config + storage schema (ETA 5d).

Ian: I'll write a short runtime notes doc for KV/streaming risks and recommended guardrails.

Lina: Thanks — assigning Lina as overall PM owner. If nobody objects, I'll lock acceptance criteria tomorrow and open the spec PR. :thumbsup:
